item.description:
Arma preview.
### From Crest - A Quick Window opened from a link in another app opens once, where it stays, without flashing or jumping, and Arma's other windows stay out of the way. - Closing that Quick Window returns you to the app the link came from, and Quick Windows open on the display you are using. - Settings pages scroll with the pointer anywhere on the page. - A test copy of Arma keeps its own sidebar width instead of changing the installed app's.

Arma preview.
### Fixed - The iPhone and iPad app builds again.
### From Crest - Move a folder to another Space from its menu, with its sub-folders, tabs and Split Views. Deleting a folder asks first and sends its tabs to the Archive. - A closed folder keeps showing the tabs that were loaded when it closed, and clicking a folder inside it opens that folder. - Split Views look and work like folders: click to collapse, double-click to rename. - Texture is now a strength from none to full, in every style. Modern has its gradient angle dial back. - The selected tab wears the window's glass, like the address field and pins. - Appearance › Material color sets whether the address field, pins and extension strip read light or dark: following the Space (the default), always light, always dark, or as the window reads. A theme's own control colors still win. - Copy URL and Site Controls sit side by side, and the sidebar can narrow further. In a narrow address field, Copy URL appears while the pointer is over it. - Appearance can show the address on two lines, on one line, or as the site alone. - Super Copy, on by default, removes trackers from links you copy or share. - The Start Page shows the app icon you picked, and its title follows the Space's colors.

Arma preview.
### New - Themes can color the address field and pins: a fill at any opacity, a text color for the site and icons, and a quieter color for the page's path. Find them in Settings › Themes › Other › Address field and pins, in a theme file's `controls` section, or with `arma theme edit --controls-…`. - The themes Arma comes with color the address field and pins to match, in light and dark looks.
### Improved - Right-clicking a link lists Open Link in New Tab and New Window first, with Arma's Space, Peek and Split View rows after them.
### From Crest 0.9.8 - Choose how much customization to see with three styles in Settings › Appearance: Heraldic (Full) keeps every control, while Modern and Simple show fewer and keep the rest under Advanced. Setup offers Simple as a look too. - Space icons in the switcher can be dots. - Text over a Space's colors is easier to read, and the address field and pins look the same on every Space unless a theme colors them.

Arma preview.
### Improved - The themes Arma comes with now color their popovers to match, in both light and dark looks.

Arma preview.
### New - Themes can color popovers such as Site Controls and Folder Appearance: background, text, secondary text, accent and its opacity, and button fill and outline. Find them in Settings › Themes › Other › Popovers, in a theme file's `popovers` section, or with `arma theme edit --popover-…`. - Popover buttons stay readable when they are unavailable.

Arma preview.
### From Crest 0.9.7 - An extension that opens its own popup, as a password manager does from a locked sign-in field, shows it over the page on Chromium. - Peek keeps working for links on pages that update their own address as you browse them. - A link that launches Arma opens in front of the windows it reopens. - Importing from Arc no longer fails for Spaces that share a profile, and the import finishes even when Arc's passwords can't be read. - The Private Browsing Space no longer offers a lock it can't keep.

Arma preview.
### Security - Chromium is updated to 157.0.8103.51, which fixes CVE-2026-125350, a security flaw being exploited in the wild, and eight other security flaws.
### From Crest 0.9.1 - A signed Arma build now proves it can load a page before it ships: packaging refuses engine helpers of an unknown kind or with the wrong entitlements, and runs the signed package's own helpers to require a page's JavaScript to run.

Arma preview.
### Arma 0.9 - Arma moves to the 0.9 line with Crest 0.9, which brings together Sub-Spaces, built-in ad blocking on Mac, iPhone and iPad, a Chromium engine built from Chromium itself at 157, and the Quick Window, Peek and appearance work. Arma's 0.8 releases already carried all of it; this build changes the version line and nothing else.

Arma preview. Chromium 157, and themes that keep their dark look.
### New - Settings › Themes has an Appearance preview that draws the windows light or dark while the page is open, so a dark look can be made and checked on a light Mac, and the other way round.
### Improved - Chromium is updated to 157.0.8103.39 with upstream security and compatibility fixes. - Turning a theme's Dark look off keeps that look, so turning it back on brings your work back instead of starting over. - A theme file keeps its dark look while the look is off, so an exported theme carries both looks. - The Themes preview draws a look in the window appearance it is worn in, so Light and Dark show the difference. - `arma theme edit --unpair-dark` keeps the theme's dark look turned off, and `--dark` turns it back on.
### Fixed - A Space keeps the same colors in light and dark windows; a light look no longer goes grey when the window is dark. - A page in Chromium that asks for protected video, such as a streaming service's player, now switches to WebKit to play it with FairPlay instead of failing in Chromium.

Arma preview.
### Fixed - `arma tab open --engine` opens the page in the engine you name, instead of leaving it in the default one.
### New - The repository carries skills for coding agents under `skills/`: setting Arma up, everyday use, the `arma` command line, themes, agent browsing and power-user settings.

Arma preview. Arma for Mac now needs macOS 15.2 instead of macOS 26.1.
### New - Arma for Mac runs on macOS 15.2 and later. This is the first build for macOS 15 and it has not been tried on a Mac running macOS 15 yet, so please report anything that looks or works wrong there. - On macOS 15, glass surfaces such as notices, the command palette and the element picker are drawn with a system material, and a page is translated when you ask rather than on its own.
Nothing changes on macOS 26 and later.

Arma preview. Brings in upstream Crest's ad blocking.
### New - Arma blocks ads and trackers on every page, in WebKit and Chromium tabs, with EasyList, EasyPrivacy, uBlock Origin's lists and a list for your language. The lists stay up to date on their own, and blocked ads leave no empty boxes. - Ad blocking has its own page in Settings and applies to every Space alike. Choose Off, Balanced or Strict, which also hides cookie notices and other annoyances. Turn single lists on or off, update them all at once, subscribe to more lists by address, and write your own rules in My Filters. - Block Element, in a page's actions, the Page menu or a right-click, hides something the lists miss. Show Blocked Elements brings it back. - Turn Off Blocking on a site from the page's actions when the site doesn't work with it. The site stays unblocked in every Space until you turn blocking on again.
### Improved - On Chromium pages, sites can no longer see which blocking rules they match or bring back what Arma hides.
### Fixed - Closing a tab while its Chromium page is full screen no longer makes Arma quit. - A full-screen Chromium page stays full screen when it moves to its next slide or video. - Settings stays smooth with hundreds of saved websites, passwords and site permissions. - Clicking the search field above saved passwords or website data lets you type in it.

Arma preview.
### Terminal - `arma tab open` places a new tab as it opens: `--pinned` or `--saved`, `--folder <path>`, and `--title` for a name of your own. - Tab and folder actions take a place in the list: `--before <row>`, `--after <row>` or `--at <n>`, where a row is a tab or a folder. `arma tab move`, `pin`, `save` and `unpin`, and `arma folder create` and `add` all take one. - `arma folder move` moves a folder, with everything in it, into another folder, to the top level, or between the saved and open tabs. - `arma theme` has one form. `arma theme edit --space <name>` changes the theme a Space uses, `arma theme use` gives it another, and `arma theme reset` puts a theme's background, icon, folders or command palette back to the plain look. The old `arma theme --space <name> [flags]` form is gone.
### Fixed - A tab filed into an empty folder joins the folder where it is, instead of carrying the folder to the end of its section. This also covers dropping a tab into an empty folder in the sidebar.

Arma preview.
### From Crest 0.8.195 - Links on Facebook, and other links with brackets in their address, open in Peek instead of a blank page or an error page. - The sidebar's rows, Space header and Space pages slide with the card when you switch Space, and choosing a Space further than next door plays one slide instead of running past the Spaces between. - The sidebar floating over the page comes out once the pointer has rested on the window's edge for a moment, stays out while the pointer is past the window on its side, and has the docked sidebar's resize handle on its edge.

Arma preview.
### From Crest 0.8.193 - New windows open at the sidebar width you last chose. - Clear Unpinned Tabs and Shift-Command-K clear only the shown Space's open tabs. Pinned and saved tabs stay, and so do other Spaces' tabs. - The inline address completion and the provider chip stop flickering while you type. - A finished download shows "Downloaded <file>" in the notice capsule. - An optional Copy URL button beside Site Controls in the address field, off by default, in Settings › Appearance › Address field. - Arma is listed in Finder's Open With menu for PDFs. - Arma stays responsive with many Spaces and extensions: session saves are coalesced, an extension refresh covers only the profile that changed, and offscreen Space pages are not rebuilt. - With Show sidebar on hover in full screen turned on, a full-screen page stays full screen when you swipe to another Space.
### Themes - A theme can give folders a highlight color and opacity of their own, the tint their rows take while a folder is open, hovered or chosen, in Settings › Themes › Folders and with `arma theme`. - Folders have one tint control: Highlight color and Highlight opacity replace the Intensity slider. Looks and themes from before keep the tint they had. - Arma ships three more themes: Textured, Heraldic and Modern, so they can be edited and put on any Space. - The Catppuccin themes' folders take their colors from each flavor's palette.

Arma preview.
### Windows - Return to Main Window works when no main window is open: it opens one, which takes the window's tabs as soon as it appears, the way a torn-off window takes its tab.
### Settings - Choosing a Space in Settings is handled by Crest's own code alone; Arma's earlier workaround for Spaces imported from Arc is gone, since Crest's fix covers the cause.
### For contributors - `AGENTS.md` now says how to fix things the way upstream Crest does: name the exact cause, make the smallest native change at that spot, and check Crest's recent commits before a larger change.

Arma preview.
### From Crest - Offer Touch ID to Chromium sites that check for it first. - Install private Chrome Web Store extensions on Chromium. - Chromium pages keep taking clicks after a drag. - Discord stays signed in on Chromium pages. - Every popover is drawn on one flyout surface, and the color grid is filled. - Clicking a Space in Settings opens its page even when the pointer moves a little during the click. - The feature tour fits every screen.
### Settings - Clicking a Space in Settings now uses Crest's own fix; the Settings sidebar is Crest's again, with the Rearrange button for reordering Spaces.
### Command line - The README shows `arma passwords`: unlock a Space's passwords with Touch ID, then list or copy them from the terminal.

Arma preview.
### Fixed - In a Quick Window's address editor, clicking or dragging in the address places the cursor or selects part of it, so you can trim a URL, instead of the whole address staying selected.

Arma preview.
### Windows - Open in New Window keeps the tab in the main window, unloaded, and opens a copy in the new window, so closing that window by mistake loses nothing. - Return to Main Window puts the copy back in the tab's place, keeping the page you moved on to.

Arma preview.
### Windows - Open in New Window on a tab moves it into a window of its own, as dragging it out of the window does. Open Link in New Window on a page opens the link in one. - A window that holds only its own tabs shows Return to Main Window at the top of its sidebar. One click moves all of its tabs back into the Space's main window, each to the folder or section it left, and closes the window. - Dragging the window from the top of a page, or from the strip beside the window buttons, is macOS's own window drag again, so pushing the window against a screen edge tiles it.
### Settings - A Space in Settings opens on the first click, shows as selected right away, and opens on its Appearance page. - Drag any Space in the Settings list onto another to make it a Sub-Space, or between Spaces to reorder. The Rearrange button is gone. - The arrow keys move through the Settings list from Space to Space.
### From Crest - A phone or security key is offered when a Chromium passkey isn't on this Mac. - Chromium extension icons show their blocked-request count. - Edit shortcuts such as Copy and Paste work in Chromium extension popups and side panels. - Arma's own picker asks when a Chromium page shares its own tab. - Windows that Chromium pages open and fill in themselves are shown. - Distant sidebar folders draw as placeholders of their height. - Shift with a number key is recorded as the number in shortcuts.

Arma preview.
### Windows - Right-click a tab and choose Open in New Window to open a new window, like the one ⌘N opens, already showing that tab. - Right-click a link and choose Open Link in New Window, under Open Link in New Tab, to open the link in a new tab shown in a new window.

Arma preview.
### Split View - Resizing Split View pages no longer leaves a white band under Chromium pages. The band grew each time the bar between pages was dragged or the split was laid out again, and stayed until the page reloaded.

Arma preview.
### Passwords - The Save password? prompt holds the email, username, password, category, notes and Include subdomains, and stays up 10 seconds unless you change it; resting the pointer on it starts the time over. - The password bubble also opens under a username or email field, closes when you click away or keep typing, and offers the generator's options on sign-up pages. - ✕ on the bubble offers to pause Arma Passwords on the tab, until resumed or for a minute up to a day; resume early from the site menu or `@passwords`. - A page's site menu has Manage Passwords, with how many the site has saved. - `arma passwords` reads and changes a Space's saved passwords from the terminal after a Touch ID or Mac password unlock that lasts an hour at most. - Changing Ask to authenticate asks you to authenticate first; new installs start at Don't Ask.
### Themes - Arc Blush ships beside Arc Sky, and Catppuccin Macchiato and JellyFish have new colors. - ⌘Z and ⇧⌘Z undo and redo edits on the Themes page. - Folders on a picture theme line up with their tabs, with even spacing above and below an open folder. - The icon picker stays readable on every theme.
### Browsing - Sites stay signed in when Arma quits and reopens, and Arma opens the tab you were on unless you choose otherwise. - When a website keeps a shortcut such as ⌘S, pressing it again runs Arma's command; choose Prefer Arma, Use Both or Prefer Website for each shortcut in Settings › Shortcuts. - The window drags from rows on pages such as GitHub's commit list that take focus but not clicks.

Arma 0.8.227 preview.
- Adding several sites in a row under Never Save Passwords On now opens each new row empty, instead of repeating the site you just added.

Arma 0.8.226 preview.
- Drag the top of a page to move the window, as in Arc, wherever nothing there takes a click; text you can select and links still work. - The Opened in Background Tab notice stays longer, waits while your pointer is on it, and offers Show Tab. Notices with a button take your click instead of the page under them. - The Save password? prompt has a close button, closes after a few seconds you can set, and offers Never for This Website. Each Space’s Passwords settings list the websites it never offers to save on, with Include subdomains per site. - Type @passwords in the command palette to find a saved login and copy its username, password or website, fill it into the page, or open the site. - Choose whether showing or copying a saved password asks you to authenticate each time, every 15 minutes, or not at all. - Check for Updates rolls out a hidden sidebar to show its answer, and @update checks from the command palette. - New Spaces start with Arma's gold and red crest.

Arma 0.8.225 preview.
- Check for Updates rolls a hidden sidebar out to show its answer, and tucks it away when you click elsewhere. - Type @update in the command palette to check for a new version. - New Spaces start with Arma's gold and red crest.

Arma 0.8.224 preview.
- When Check for Updates finds an update, the sidebar opens so you can see it.

Arma 0.8.223 preview.
- Check for Updates works: Arma finds and installs new releases on its own from this version on. - Servo is left out of this preview while it is made stable. Tabs, site rules and defaults set to Servo open in Chromium. - Open a Quick Window from any app with its shortcut. - Notices, status colours and controls are shared across Arma. - Brings in the latest Crest changes.
